newsitem.title: FRANCE: French dustman sues doctor over "AIDS syringes".
newsitem.headline: French dustman sues doctor over "AIDS syringes".

text.p: A French dustman who said he was infected with AIDS while handling a bag containing used syringes asked a court on Monday to order the doctor who threw out the needles to pay him three million francs ($526,000) in damages.
Franck Salvatore, 34, hurt his hand while picking up a plastic rubbish bag at a Paris market on May 25, 1991.

The bag, which contained needles and blood samples among other waste, came from the office of Roland Sananes, a physician specialising in acupuncture, and had been dropped at the market by the concierge of his building.
The following September, a transfusion centre where Salvatore had regularly donated blood for years, told him he was infected with the AIDS virus.
Salvatore's lawyer Nicole Denoits-Blanc told the court her client's blood had tested negatively for AIDS at the transfusion centre the day before the accident.
"The doctor committed an exceptional personal error, lacking caution, good sense and violating rules on medical waste," she said.

Professor Luc Montagnier, the scientist credited with discovering the AIDS virus, appeared in court as an expert witness, saying it was unlikely Salvatore was contaminated by the disposed syringes. He said this could have happened only with a large, hollow needle, a deep wound or a considerable amount of blood.
Sananes' lawyer Dominique Cresseaux said the evidence was insufficient because the needle in question had never been found and there was no proof it came from the doctor's office.
The Paris municipality, Salvatore's employer, is also demanding 20,000 francs ($3,500) in damages from Sananes.
The court will give its verdict on May 5.
